speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a matter close to residents and I believe some of my fellow Parliamentarians in this House.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This Adjournment Motion is not not in opposition to commerce, enterprise or progress.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Nor is it an attempt to pit residents against businesses.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Their efforts often involve difficult trade-offs, difficult situations; and I thank them for navigating these with professionalism and care.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also wish to pay tribute to the late Dr Liu Thai Ker, who passed away on 18 January 2026 this year.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Often described as the father of urban planning in Singapore, Dr Liu wisely reminded us that cities exist first and foremost to serve the people who live in them, not merely for aesthetics or for economic efficiency.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Dr Liu emphasised quality of life, dignity and community well-being as the ultimate goals of urban planning.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: At the same time, he also recognised that a good city must support livelihoods and enterprise, not suppress them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Singapore’s residential neighbourhoods are meant to be safe and family-friendly environments, homes for our people, while at the same time remaining economically active and inclusive.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many residents of ours embrace the vision of mixed-use neighbourhoods with shops, cafés and services such as preschools, Active Ageing Centers at their doorsteps.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They hope for convenience, vibrancy and a more connected community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Indeed, when done well, such commercial activity adds value, creates jobs and strengthens neighbourhood life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, when intensity, scale or behaviour crosses certain thresholds, tensions can arise, not because this mixed-use model is flawed, but because the safeguards have not kept pace with lived realities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some are more sensitive to disturbance than others and can make unreasonable demands.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But many other residents recognise that well-run businesses add vibrancy and convenience to residential estates.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, when these commercial activities intensify without adequate planning or safeguards, even these residents experience persistent day-to-day challenges.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Challenges such as noise and smell, continuous noise from exhaust fans, amplified music, late-night operations as well as cooking odours from kitchen vents, can travel into common residential areas and upper-floor homes, affecting residents’ rest and living comfort.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Residents have also raised concerns about how certain ground-floor businesses operate in close proximity to homes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: During my house visits, for example in the Crawford estate, families and seniors shared that visible solicitation activities outside some massage establishments made walking home very uncomfortable.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Not just the wives, but also the husbands felt uncomfortable.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While some of these premises have since vacated, my residents at Crawford remain anxious about what types of businesses may subsequently replace or occupy these spaces.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many Members will also be familiar with the reported situation at Tanjong Pagar Complex under the hon Member Mr Foo Cexiang.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Member Ms Cassandra Lee also had appealed recently for assistance to counter vice activities in licensed massage establishments.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Queues, waste disposal issues and competition for parking between residents and patrons can strain hygiene standards and create friction in otherwise peaceful neighbourhoods.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to stress that these challenges that I have mentioned would have been far worse without the dedication of frontline agencies and responsible businesses who make genuine efforts to comply and be good neighbours.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of these business operators also provide essential services and are even part of our Community Development Council Voucher Scheme.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, despite existing frameworks and good intentions on all sides, some disamenities persist.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: From conversations with residents, businesses and enforcement agencies, I see four underlying reasons why current safeguards fall short.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Under the Massage Establishments Exemption Order 2018, premises that provide massage services in full public view are exempted from licensing and any regulatory oversight.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They are only required to notify the licensing officer of their name and address before commencing operations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Unlike fully licensed operators, they are not subject to the same operational conditions or compliance requirements.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In practice, this regulatory light-touch has allowed a proliferation of outlets that contribute to neighbourhood disamenities, without adequate safeguards for residents or meaningful accountability.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Enforcement responsibilities currently are often divided across agencies: licensing authorities for food, entertainment or massage; building management and estate maintenance; environmental health for noise or odour; and urban planning bodies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Crucially, the cumulative neighbourhood impact is often insufficiently assessed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While zoning controls exist, they tend to operate at a broad, area-based level.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They may not adequately account for hyper-local conditions such as the over-concentration of certain commercial activities within a single block or single precinct.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is unclear whether licensing or landlord agencies consistently factor in business clustering effects when such approvals are granted.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What may be acceptable in isolation can, when concentrated, significantly erode residential amenities and community well-being.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Reason 4: consequences that do not deter poor behaviour.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: When penalties do not meaningfully affect business viability or impose operational consequences, there is little incentive for genuine behavioural or structural change.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Without credible deterrence, enforcement risks becoming reactive and repetitive, penalising the same offenders without delivering lasting relief to our residents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to speak next about a balanced framework of prevention, governance and enforcement.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a cat-and-mouse exercise that frustrates residents, burdens agencies and creates uncertainty for businesses.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I therefore urge the Government to consider a more integrated framework of prevention, governance, enforcement – one intended to be practical and predictable, not punitive.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It gives clarity to businesses upfront, supports early resolution between residents and business operators on the ground, and reserves enforcement for persistent non-compliance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Factors such as operating hours, alcohol service, music amplification, likelihood of late-night congregation and proximity to homes or schools should be taken into account.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This gives businesses clear signals upfront and allows planning decisions to better reflect lived reality at the block or precinct level, rather than broad zoning assumptions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For higher-impact uses in residential areas, a simple, structured consultation at the pre-approval stage can help surface risks early.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of us Members of Parliament have had to assist innocent business operators who unknowingly either signed tenancy agreements assuming licences were transferable or automatic; or they have committed substantial investments before being informed that their proposed use was already under heightened scrutiny or under policy review.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A clearly scoped consultation process, similar in nature, in principle to the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority's Long-Term Visit Pass consultation framework or checklist helps to clarify regulatory expectations upfront, reduce costly missteps for businesses, minimise future disputes with residents and lower the likelihood of enforcement, appeals, or litigation downstream.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It improves investment certainty and protects livelihoods for businesses, while also reducing distress for our residents and enforcement burdens for agencies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Existing legislation should be reviewed to ensure that all commercial activities that affect residential amenity are subject to basic, enforceable standards.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is not about over-regulation, but about ensuring that regulatory light-touch does not become a blind spot.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I just read in the papers, I am so glad that the Ministry of Home Affairs is currently looking into these gaps.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Second, on governance, managing day-to-day realities on the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This provides a practical way to resolve issues early, without immediately resorting to enforcement.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: At the community level, some of us already give out Good Neighbour Awards to residents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We should consider extending similar recognition to commercial neighbours who consistently demonstrate responsible behaviour and explore benefits such as greater flexibility in outdoor dining or longer renewal extensions for those with strong compliance records.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This reinforces the message that good behaviour is rewarded, not just bad behaviour punished.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A shared single case view across planning, licensing, environmental health, estate management and public order agencies would allow patterns to be seen earlier, rather than each issue being handled in reaction, in isolation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This improves fairness, reduces duplication and helps agencies act with consistency and institutional memory.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My last proposal is related to enforcement – firm, but proportionate enforcement.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Enforcement should focus on repeated and substantiated non-compliance, not isolated lapses by responsible operators.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This approach provides certainty for businesses, protects well-run operators from unfair competition and allows agencies to focus on the small minority that repeatedly undermine neighbourhood liveability.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Shops, cafés, services bring convenience, they bring jobs, they bring life to our estates.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many business operators invest their savings, employ local workers and genuinely want to be good neighbours.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We should support, not penalise, these responsible businesses.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And we should also not condone residents who are unreasonable.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I look forward to the Government’s favourable consideration of the proposals that I have put up to protect our residents’ well-being while sustaining vibrant, responsible commercial activity in the neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many residents value having shops, eateries and entertainment options close to home, as they bring convenience and vibrancy to daily life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A coffee shop downstairs can mean a quick bite anytime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nearby entertainment options offer spaces for friends and families to gather and to socialise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These businesses play an important role in serving community needs and often add value to homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, I fully agree with the Member that because these activities operate close to homes, they need to be carefully managed to ensure that they remain compatible with residential living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Government agencies therefore work together to plan, regulate and license commercial activities to balance community needs and residents’ well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In some cases, such as commercially run shopping malls or privately-owned HDB shops, market forces determine the mix of shops while adhering to regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Member has shared challenges faced by residents arising from noise, smell, hygiene and concerns on safety, caused by commercial activity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: She has also proposed some measures with regard to legislative coverage, planning and enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will share how Government agencies plan, gatekeep and enforce rules for commercial activities to balance the needs of both residents and business operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: URA considers where and what type of businesses can be located, knowing that different businesses can affect residents differently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most businesses benefit residents and cause little disturbance, like retail shops and medical clinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: URA will continue to plan for such types of commercial activity to better serve residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There is also demand for other businesses, such as nightlife venues and massage establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most nightlife establishments like bars and karaoke lounges are situated away from residential areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nightlife establishments are not allowed in both sold and rental HDB shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: New nightlife establishments are also not allowed within commercial developments integrated with residential units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Government agencies will continue to work closely with grassroots advisors to manage local concentration issues and will not hesitate to turf out unsavoury operators who do not adhere to regulations or tenancy conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Massage establishments such as sports massage, chiropractor clinics and Traditional Chinese Medicine clinics, if properly regulated, provide wellness services that residents value, which is why they are allowed to operate in the heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That said, HDB imposes planning and trade mix controls on heartland shops to strike a balance between having a vibrant commercial landscape and preserving the residential character of our HDB heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB maintains a published list of allowable uses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Any change of use must first obtain HDB’s approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For massage establishments, HDB sets quotas to regulate their numbers in each estate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond determining where businesses can locate, agencies also have approval mechanisms to assess who can operate and under what conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Licensing serves as a gatekeeping tool to assess operator suitability and establish operational requirements to manage and to mitigate potential disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nightlife establishments and massage establishments are regulated by the SPF and the licensing framework ensures that these venues are not misused for vice activities and to minimise law and order concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During the licence application process, SPF conducts background checks on applicants, including reviews of their general records for links to errant establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I note the Member’s comments on the disamenities caused by open concept massage establishments which are exempted from licensing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Industry consultation will be done in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond licensing, agencies use tenancy conditions as an additional lever to mitigate disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, food establishments such as coffee shops and small eateries are often located near residential areas to serve residents’ daily needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For food establishments operating in HDB estates, HDB imposes tenancy conditions to manage potential disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, to minimise noise, HDB requires coffee shops to stop the use of outdoor refreshment areas by 11.00 pm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To control odour issues and to maintain hygiene, coffee shops are required to install appropriate exhaust systems and grease traps, and to implement proper waste management practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where new business models with new products and new service offerings emerge to challenge existing regulations and trade mix controls, agencies will review the relevant frameworks to strike a balance between protecting residents from disamenities and preserving business viability and entrepreneurship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Moving on to enforcement, there is no one-size-fits-all approach as it involves real-world operations with multiple stakeholders and varying circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Agencies actively monitor businesses and take calibrated but firm action when issues arise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When repeated issues arise, we trigger tighter conditions and stronger enforcement action using planning, licensing and tenancy levers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, agencies strive to work closely together on enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, URA works with agencies to adopt a three-strikes approach to deal with problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When a business flouts any rules or requirements, they will receive a warning letter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For food establishments operating in HDB estates, HDB takes into account the feedback received by different agencies when assessing tenancy and tenancy renewals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, HDB works with the National Environment Agency when there is feedback on noise and other environmental concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB also takes into account feedback provided to the SPF regarding law and order concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most operators have been cooperative when HDB steps in to remind them of their tenancy conditions and the feedback received.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where warranted, agencies have taken firm joint enforcement action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SPF will continue to conduct enforcement checks and ensure public entertainment outlets and massage establishments comply with the rules and regulations and take strict action against errant operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the Member's suggestion for structured pre-approval consultation, this is consistent with agencies' broader objective of providing greater clarity and transparency upfront.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, applicants are provided with information on relevant planning parameters, licensing requirements and tenancy conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These set out the types of activities permitted and the operating standards expected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Agencies will continue to look at how to make these information clearer and more transparent upfront for applicants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also thank the Member for her suggestion regarding Good Neighbour Agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We would encourage it at the grassroots level as a way to establish good social norms and community relations between local businesses and residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To conclude, the Government is committed to maintaining liveable neighbourhoods through proper planning, careful gatekeeping and firm enforcement when needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to achieve the best balance for both residents and business operators and we welcome the Member's suggestions to do this even better.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is to avoid the rush and stress of meeting the closing deadline for cuts.
